answer.rationale: Degradation is confined to the primary region, which most closely matches the regional failover pattern (memory_b2); failover is also fully reversible and protects in-flight writes better than a mid-peak rollback. The release correlation (memory_b1) makes rollback a credible alternative, so I flag both for verification before committing; if the archive shows failover risks write loss at peak settlement, I would pivot to rollback_release. Rolling back a release during peak write traffic carries its own risk of dropped or duplicated writes, so I prefer failover with the primary kept warm for rapid failback.
